# gtk4's widgets under --simulate with the per-class protocol: the interpreter
# makes, fills and connects each node through the #[gen.protocol] functions
# lowering splices into the target's node ops, so the GTK natives they call are
# stubbed and handed the `c.str`s CMarshal converts their strings to. Each is
# freed by ReleaseTemps after the call that read it -- a reactive label's text
# on every write, a link button's uri and its constructor's "" -- and a
# switch's notify is connected through gtk4rt, which makes none.

env PATH=

sngl test --simulate gtk4 app.sngl
stdout '^ok   1 tests, 0 failures$'
! stdout 'leak'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:test"
import go "sngl:language/go"
import gtk "gir:Gtk-4.0"

output {
    go {
        gtk4(gir="builtin", cgo=true)
    }
}

component page ui.node {
    var n = 0
    var on = false

    ui.vbox {
        ui.text("{n}")
        gtk.GtkLinkButton(uri="https://example.com", label="site")
        gtk.GtkSwitch(@notifyActive {
            on = !on
        })
        ui.button(text="more", @click {
            n = n + 1
        })
    }
}

func testCounts(t test.Test, c page) {
    c.n = 2
    c.n = 3
    t.assert(c.n == 3)
}

ui.window(title="t") {
    page
}
